course_descriptions.title: Design Project
course_descriptions.description: These courses are intended to impart training in design of product/ process or other artifact to the students in the discipline or interdisciplinary areas. These courses are normally available to students in third or higher levels. These courses must coterminate with project reports.

course_descriptions.title: Plasma Physics and its Applications
course_descriptions.description: Introduction to plasma physics. Motion of single charged particles in Electric and Magnetic fields. Fluid description of plasma and study of waves in plasmas, Theory of instabilities in plasma, A Kinetic theory description of plasma and some basic plasma phenomenon, Applications of plasma physics to plasma based accelerators, plasma based energy radiation sources, magnetic confinement fusion, laser-plasma interaction, astrophysical plasma, and studying plasma physics using computer simulation.

course_descriptions.title: Thin Film Technology
course_descriptions.description: Overview of thin film technology, Structure and bonding of materials, Defects in thin film, Thermodynamics and phase diagram, Kinetics and diffusion mechanism, Surface nucleation and film growth, Epitaxy and growth modes, Basics of vacuum science and technology, Thin film growth technology, Epitaxial growth techniques, Structure and morphology of thin films, Surface reconstruction and surface chemistry, Electrical and magnetic properties, Special topics on thin film application, Laboratory based experiments or assignments related to thin films.

course_descriptions.title: Introduction to Quantum Field Theory
course_descriptions.description: Klein-Gordan equation, SU(2) and rotation group, SL(2,C) and Lorentz Group, antiparticles, construction of Dirac Spinors, algebra of gamma matrices, Maxwell and Proca equations, Maxwell's equations and differential geometry; Lagrangian Formulation of particle mechanics, real scalar field and Noether's theorem, real and complex scalar fields, Yang-Mills field, geometry of gauge fields, cannonical quantization of Klein-Gordan, Dirac and Electromagnetic field, spontaneously broken gauge symmetries, Goldstone theorem, superconductivity.

course_descriptions.title: Particle Physics
course_descriptions.description: Klein-Gordan equation, time-dependent non-relativistic perturbation theory, spinless electron-muon scattering and electron-positron scattering, crossing symmetry, Dirac equation, standard examples of scattering, parity violation and V-A interaction, beta decay, muon decay, weak neutral currents, Cabibo angle, weak mixing angles, CP violation, Weak isospin and hypercharge, basic electroweak interaction, Lagrangian and single particle waveequation, U(1) local gauge invariance and QED, non-abelian gauge invariance and QCD, spontaneous symmetry breaking, Higgs mechanism, spontaneous breaking of local SU(2) gauge symmetry.

course_descriptions.title: Physics of Advanced Materials
course_descriptions.description: Review of fundamentals of crystallography, structural properties of crystals, polymers and glasses, processes involved in materials preparation, viz., diffusion, phase diagrams, advanced techniques to prepare low dimensional systems and thin films, kinetics of phase transformations, Mechanical, structural, thermal and electrical characterization of advanced materials, e.g., high Tc superconductors, superionic conductors, conducting polymers, dielectrics, ferroelectric materials, polycrystalline semiconducting materials, magnetic semiconductors, magneto resistance and GMR materials, shape memory alloys.

course_descriptions.title: General Theory of Relativity and Cosmology
course_descriptions.description: Review of relativistic mechanics, gravity as geometry, descriptions of curved space-time, tensor analysis, geodesic equations, affine connections, parallel transport, Riemann and Ricci tensors, Einstein’s equations, Schwarzschild solution, classic tests of general theory of relativity, mapping the universe, Friedmann-Robertson-Walker (FRW) cosmological model, Friedmann equation and the evolution of the universe, thermal history of the early universe, shortcomings of standard model of cosmology, theory of inflation, cosmic microwave background radiations (CMBR), baryogenesis, dark matter & dark energy.

course_descriptions.title: Soft Condensed Matter Physics
course_descriptions.description: Forces, energies, timescale and dimensionality in soft condensed matter, phase transition, mean field theory and its breakdown, simulation of Ising spin using Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics, colloidal dispersion, polymer physics, molecular order in soft condensed matter – i) liquid crystals ii) polymer, supramolecular self assembly.

course_descriptions.title: Experimental Methods of Physics
course_descriptions.description: Vacuum techniques, sample preparation techniques, X-ray diffraction, scanning probe microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, low temperature techniques, magnetic measurements, VI- Mossbauer and positron annihilation spectroscopy, neutron diffraction, Rutherford backscattering, techniques in nuclear experimentation, high energy accelerators.

course_descriptions.title: Lasers and Applications
course_descriptions.description: Properties of laser light, theories of some simple optical processes, basic principles of lasers, solid-state lasers, gas lasers, semiconductor lasers, free electron lasers, liquid, dye and chemical lasers, dynamics of laser processes, advances in laser physics, Q-switching, modelocking (active and passive), saturable absorbers, Kerr lens mode locking, non-linear optics, laser spectroscopy, time resolved spectroscopy, multi-photon spectroscopy.

course_descriptions.title: Advanced Solid State Physics
course_descriptions.description: Schrodinger field theory (second quantized formalism), Bose and Fermi fields, equivalence with many body quantum mechanics, particles and holes, single particle Green functions and propagators, diagrammatic techniques, application to Fermi systems (electrons in a metal, electron – phonon interaction) and Bose systems (superconductivity, superfluidity).

course_descriptions.title: Quantum Optics
course_descriptions.description: Quantization of the electromagnetic field, single mode and multimode fields, vacuum fluctuations and zero-point energy, coherent states, atom - field interaction - semiclassical and quantum, the Rabi model, Jaynes-Cummings model, beam splitters and interferometry, squeezed states, lasers.

course_descriptions.title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics
course_descriptions.description: Symmetries, conservation laws and degeneracies; Discrete symmetries - parity, lattice translations and time reversal; Identical particles, permutation symmetry, symmetrization postulate, twoelectron system, the helium atom; Scattering theory - Lippman- Schwinger equation, Born approximation, optical theorem, eikonal approximation, method of partial waves; Quantum theory of radiation - quantization of electromagnetic field, interaction of electromagnetic radiation with atoms; relativistic quantum mechanics.

course_descriptions.title: Group Theory and Applications
course_descriptions.description: Basic concepts – group axioms and examples of groups, subgroups, cosets, invariant subgroups; group representation – unitary representation, irreducible representation, character table, Schur’s lemmas; the point symmetry group and applications to molecular and crystal structure; Continuous groups – Lie groups, infinitesimal transformation, structure constants; Lie algebras, irreducible representations of Lie groups and Lie algebras; linear groups, rotation groups, groups of the standard model of particle physics.

course_descriptions.title: Special Topics in Statistical Mechanics
course_descriptions.description: The Ising Model – Definition, equivalence to other models, spontaneous magnetization, Bragg- William approximation, Bethe-Peierls Approximation, one dimensional Ising model, exact solution in one and two dimensions; Landau’s mean field theory for phase transition – the order parameter, correlation function and fluctuation-dissipation theorem, critical exponents, calculation of critical exponents, scale invariance, field driven transitions, temperature driven condition, Landau-Ginzberg theory, two-point correlation function, Ginzberg criterion, Gaussian approximation; Scaling hypothesis – universality and universality classes, renormalization group; Elements of nonequilibrium statistical mechanics – Brownian motion, diffusion and Langevin equation, relation between dissipation and fluctuating force, Fokker-Planck equation.

course_descriptions.title: Advanced Electrodynamics
course_descriptions.description: Review of Maxwell’s equations – Maxwell’s equations, scalar and vector potentials, gauge transformations of the potentials, the electromagnetic wave equation, retarded and advanced Green’s functions for the wave equation and their interpretation, transformation properties of electromagnetic fields; Radiating systems – multipole expansion of radiation fields, energy and angular momentum of multipole radiation, multipole radiation in atoms and nuclei, multipole radiation from a linear, centre-fed antenna; Scattering and diffraction – perturbation theory of scattering, scattering by gases and liquids, scattering of EM waves by a sphere, scalar and vector diffraction theory, diffraction by a circular aperture; Dynamics of relativistic particles and EM fields – Lagrangian of a relativistic charged particle in an EM field, motion in uniform, static electromagnetic fields, Lagrangian of the EM fields, solution of wave equation in covariant form, invariant Green’s functions; Collisions, energy loss and scattering of a charged particle, Cherenkov radiation, the Bremsstrahlung; Radiation by moving charges – Lienard-Wiechert potentials and fields, Larmor’s formula and its relativistic generalization; Radiation damping – radiative reaction force from conservation of energy, Abraham-Lorentz model. PHYF425 Advanced Mathematical Methods ofPhysics 3 1 4 Course description is to be developed.

course_descriptions.title: Physics of Semiconductor Devices
course_descriptions.description: Course description is to be developed.

course_descriptions.title: Atmospheric Physics
course_descriptions.description: Course description is to be developed.

course_descriptions.title: Quantum Information Theory
course_descriptions.description: Classical Information, probability and information measures, methods of open quantum systems using density operator formalism, quantum operations, Kraus operators. Measurement and information, Entropy and information, data compression, channel capacity, Resource theory of quantum correlations and coherence, and some current issues.

course_descriptions.title: Geometrical Methods in Physics
course_descriptions.description: Manifolds, tensors, differential forms and examples from Physics, Riemannian geometry, relevance of topology to Physics, integration on a manifold, Gauss theorem and Stokes’ theorem using integrals of differential forms, fibre bundles and connections, applications of geometrical methods in Classical and Quantum Mechanics, Electrodynamics, Gravitation, and Quantum field theory.

course_descriptions.title: Classical Theory of Fields: A Symmetry Per-
course_descriptions.description: spective Rotations in real complex and Minkowski spaces laying group theoretical basis of 3-tensors and 4 tensors and spinors, transition from a discrete to continuous system, stress energy tensor, relativistic field theory, Noether’s theorem, tensor and spinor fields as representation of Lorentz group, action for spin-0 and spin-1/2, and super-symmetric multiplet, introduction of spin-1, spin-2 and spin-3/2 through appropriate local symmetries of spin-0 and spin- 1/2 actions.

course_descriptions.title: Topics in Nonlinear Optics
course_descriptions.description: Lorentz model for various order nonlinearities, properties of tensor elements; Second order processes (second harmonic generation, Pockels effect, optical parametric oscillator); phase matching in crystals; Third order processes (third harmonic generation, phase conjugation, Kerr effect, self-phase modulation, Raman effect, Stimulated Raman scattering (Stokes / anti-Stokes), Stimulated Brillouin scattering); Light interaction with plasma (waves in plasmas, Landau damping, absorption of light by inverse Bremsstrahlung, resonance absorption, two plasmon absorption, parametric decay, stimulated Raman scattering, stimulated Brillouin scattering); Concepts of ponderomotive force / energy, second harmonic generation in plasma, self-focussing, above threshold ionization, odd harmonic generation, optical field ionization, Coulomb explosion; Applications : Holography (low intensity), optical solitons (medium intensity), inertial confinement fusion (high intensity) and acceleration of charged particles with light (ultra-high intensity).
course_descriptions.prerequisites_text: PHY F212 & PHY F213

course_descriptions.title: Foundations of Quantum Mechanics
course_descriptions.description: A review of pre-quantum (classical) theories from the lens of determinism, locality, ontology, measurement, and abstract spaces; A discussion on Bell’s generic formulation of locality and ontological issues through gauge redundancy in the description of electrodynamics; Review basic quantum theory and develop a toolbox for simple quantum examples to be used later to address the issues of locality, ontology and measurement; The measurement problem; the locality problem; the ontology problem; Copenhagen VIinterpretation; Bohm’s Pilot wave theory; Bell’s theorem; many world interpretations.
course_descriptions.prerequisites_text: PHY F242: Quantum Mechanics I

course_descriptions.title: Advanced Computational Physics
course_descriptions.description: Molecular dynamics, Monte Carlo methods and its applications to various systems, cellular automata, complex systems, fractals, Discrete and fast Fourier transform, partial differential equations, FDTD, computational fluid dynamics.
course_descriptions.prerequisites_text: PHY F313: Computational Physics

course_descriptions.title: Space Science Instrumentation
course_descriptions.description: Space environment: Vacuum (very low pressure), Thermal environment and thermal design, Solar spectrum and effects on measurements/instruments, Other sources of radiation, Galactic rays, Radiation environment and its effect on measurements/instruments, Plasma and charged particle environment, Meteoroid environment, Review of relevant physical processes: secondary electron emission (SEE), ion-surfaceinteractions, photoemission, ionization, particle and photon scattering,Materials for space instruments: CTE, outgassing, mass loss, radiation damage, various properties and limitations,Detectors: Photon detectors, Particle detectors,Space Instruments: Dust detectors and analyzers, Magnetometers, UV spectrometers, IR instruments (thermal imaging, spectrometers), Imaging/cameras, Neutral/ion mass spectrometers, Plasma instruments (Faraday cups, solar wind analyzers, energetic particle detectors, Neutral particles (high and low

course_descriptions.title: Scientific Computing and Data Analysis
course_descriptions.description: Introduction to Scientific Computing: Review of programming language - C/C++, Matlab and Mathematica, The Role of Statistics in Machine Learning, Statistical Machine Learning Techniques, Advanced Statistical and Machine Learning: Foundations and Unsupervised Learning,Advanced Statistics and Machine Learning: Regression and Classification, Data Acquisition and Image Processing, Performance Modelling, Vectorisation and GPU Programming, Advanced Algorithms and Discrete Systems, Compu-

course_descriptions.title: Fundamentals of Quantum Field Theory
course_descriptions.description: Systems of identical particles and the symmetrization postulate; Second quantization – Nonrelativistic theory of identical bosons and fermions; Transition from a system with discrete degrees of freedom to continuous degrees of freedom; Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulation for a classical real and complex scalar field; Symmetries and Conversation laws; Canonical Quantization of the Schrodinger, relativistic real and relativistic complex scalar field; Correlation functions, S-matrix and its perturbative expansion; Wick’s theorem and Feynman diagrams & rules; Processes in scalar field theories at the lowest order.
course_descriptions.prerequisites_text: PHY F211: Classical Mechanics and PHY F212: Electromagnetic Theory I and PHY F241: Electromagnetic Theory II and PHY F242: Quantum Mechanics I and PHY F311: Quantum Mechanics II PHY F311: Quantum Mechanics II

course_descriptions.title: Special Project
course_descriptions.description: This is an unstructured open-ended course where under the overall supervision of an instructor-in-charge, batches of students will be attached to different instructors. Each batch will work on a specific time-bound project which is of basic or peripheral concern of his discipline. Each student must submit a project report as a culmination of his endeavour and investigation. The instructor- incharge will determine the choice of the project and also whether or not the project report is to be submitted jointly by a group or individually by a student. The course will aim to evaluate student's actual ability to use the fundamentals of knowledge and to meet new unknown situations as demonstrated by the students' interaction with the instructors and instructor-in- charge and aggregated in the project report. The instructor-in- charge may assign specific hours for formal brain-storming sessions.

course_descriptions.title: Theoretical Physics
course_descriptions.description: Calculus of Variations and its applications to Lagrangian and Hamiltonian Dynamics, Thermodynamics and Geometric Optics and Electrodynamics. Geometric and Group theoretic foundations of Hamiltonian Dynamics, Hamilton-Jacobi Theory, Integrability and Action-Angle Variables, Adiabatic Invariants, Transformation (Lie) Groups and Classical Mechanics. Modern Theory of Phase Transitions and Critical Phenomenon: Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics of Phase Transitions, General Properties (eg Scaling, Universality, Critical exponents) and Order of Phase Transitions; Introduction to Landau-Ginzburg (Mean Field Theory) theory for Second Order Phase Transitions, the Ising Model and some Examples, Phase Transitions as a symmetry-breaking phenomenon.

course_descriptions.title: Advanced Quantum Field Theory
course_descriptions.description: Diagrammatics : Feynman diagrams & rules, Loop diagrams, Smatrix, Path integrals, Gauge theories, QED and QCD Lagrangians, Renormalization group, Non-perturbative states.

course_descriptions.title: Classical Electrodynamics
course_descriptions.description: Review of Electrostatics, Magnetostatics, and solution of Boundary Value Problems. Method of Images. Maxwell equations for time dependent fields, Propagation of electromagnetic waves in unbounded media. Waveguides & Cavity Resonators. Absorption, Scattering and Diffraction, Special Relativity, Covariant formulation of Classical Electrodynamics. Dynamics of charged particles in electromagnetic fields. Radiation by moving charges and Cerenkov Radiation.

course_descriptions.title: Quantum Theory and Applications
course_descriptions.description: Mathematics of linear vector spaces, Postulates of Quantum Mechanics, Review of exactly solvable bound state problems, WKB methods, Angular momentum, Spin, Addition of angular momenta, Systems with many degrees of freedom, Perturbation theory, Scattering theory, Dirac equation.

course_descriptions.title: Condensed Matter Physics
course_descriptions.description: Free electron models, Reciprocal lattice, Electrons in weak periodic potential, Tight-binding method, Semiclassical model of electron dynamics, Theory of conduction in metals, Theory of harmonic crystals, Anharmonic effects, Semiconductors, Diamagnetism and paramagnetism, Superconductivity.

course_descriptions.title: Statistical Physics & Applications
course_descriptions.description: Liouville’s theorem, Boltzmann transport equation, H-Theorem; Postulate of statistical Mechanics; Temperature; Entropy; Microcanonical, Canonical, Grand-canonical ensembles - Derivation, calculation of macroscopic quantities, fluctuations, equivalence of ensembles, Applications, Ideal gases, Gibbs Paradox; Quantum mechanical ensemble theory; Bose-Einstein statistics –derivation, Bose Einstein condensation, applications; Fermi-Dirac Statistics – derivation, applications - Equation of state of ideal Fermi gas, Landau Diamagnetism, etc; Radiation; Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics; Interacting systems – cluster expansion, Ising model in 1-d & 2-d; Liquid Helium, phase transitions and renormalization group.

course_descriptions.title: Topics in Mathematical Physics
course_descriptions.description: Functions of complex variables, special functions, fourier analysis, sturm-Liuoville theory, partial differential equation with examples, Greens functions, Group theory, differential forms, approximation methods in solutions of PDE’s, vector valued PDE’s.

course_descriptions.title: Computational Methods in Physics
course_descriptions.description: Basics of computer programming; errors and stability of methods; Numerical techniques for: differentiation, integration, root finding, interpolation, solving linear equations, matrix inversion & diagonalization, solving ODEs & PDEs, spectral methods and Monte Carlo methods; Applications: ID Schrodinger equation, Diffusion, Vibration of strings, Ising model, 3-body problem, Chaotic systems, Electronic structure of atoms. Power spectrum of a driven pendulum, Laplace equation, Wave equation, Scattering problems. (This course is meant for PhD Students as a part of their course work)

course_descriptions.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
course_descriptions.description: Course description for the above course is to be developed.

course_descriptions.title: Selected Topics in Solid State Physics
course_descriptions.description: Schrodinger Field Theory (2nd Quantized formalism), Bose and Fermi fields, equivalence with many body quantum mechanics, particles and holes, Single particle Green functions and propagators, Diagrammatic techniques, Application to Fermi systems electrons in a metal, electron-phonon interaction) and Bose systems (superconductivity, superfluidity).

course_descriptions.title: Physics of Semiconductor Devices
course_descriptions.description: Electrons and Phonons in Crystals; Carrier dynamics in semiconductors; Junctions in semiconductors (including metals and insulators); Heterostructures; Quantum wells and Low-dimensional systems; Tunnelling transport; Optoelectronics properties; Electric and magnetic fields; The 2d Electron gas; Semiconductor spintronic devices B.E. Robotics and Industrial Automation

course_descriptions.title: Materials and Mechanics for Robotics
course_descriptions.description: Structure of Materials (Metals, Polymers, Ceramics & Composites), Novel advanced materials such as Shape memory alloys, Semiconductors, piezo-electric materials, Self-healing materials, 3D printed materials. Static equilibrium, Introduction to Stress and strain, deformation of body under axial, torsional and bending stresses, introduction to buckling.

course_descriptions.title: Introduction to Mechanisms and Robotics
course_descriptions.description: Mechanisms Fundamentals: Overview of mechanisms: linkages, gears, cams, and other mechanical systems; Degrees of freedom and mobility analysis; Grashof's law and classification of four-bar linkages; Position, velocity, and acceleration analysis of planar mechanisms. Kinematics of Robots: Introduction to robotic systems; configurations, links, and joints; Denavit-Hartenberg (D-H) parameters and transformations; Forward and inverse kinematics for robotic manipulators.

course_descriptions.title: Foundations of Data Structures and
course_descriptions.description: Algorithms Algorithm Analysis – Mathematical preliminaries, Sorting Algorithms, Search Algorithms, Linear Structures, Non-Linear Structures, Hashing, Non-Linear Structures, Graphs and Algorithms. Equivalent: BITS F232: Foundations of Data Structures and Algorithms.

course_descriptions.title: Sensors, Actuators and Signal
course_descriptions.description: Conditioning Introduction to Sensors and Transducers, Mathematical models of Transducers zero, first and second order systems, Sensing Technologies in Robotics and Industrial Automation, Actuators and mechanisms, Signal Conditioning, Conversion, Amplification and filtering using Operational amplifiers, Signal Converters and Data Acquisition System, Sensor fusion techniques using Kalman and Extended Kalman filter, Signal Conditioning Circuits for Industrial Applications and case study examples.

course_descriptions.title: Artificial Intelligence for Robotics
course_descriptions.description: Introduction to AI, Application of AI in Robotics. Introduction to Robot Operating Systems (ROS), Python and programming with application of Raspberry-Pi and Arduino. Practical Robot Design Process, implementation of pick and place process. Basic robot sensing techniques (Vision and Listening), Beam Models of Range Finders, sensor models. Object Recognition Using Neural Networks and Supervised Learning. Robot learning process, Reinforcement learning and Genetic Algorithms. Basic concepts of speech recognition and natural language. Path planning, SLAM, decision trees, classification techniques, wave front, the A* (A star) and D* (D star) algorithms, and node-based planners. Nondeterministic simulation technique and Monte Carlo modeling, the Robot Emotion Engine, the Human Emotion Model. Equivalent: BITS F327: Artificial Intelligence for Robotics.

course_descriptions.title: Control Systems
course_descriptions.description: Modeling and classification of dynamical systems, Proper-ties and advantages of feedback systems, time-domain analysis, frequency-domain analysis, stability and performance analysis, State space analysis, controller design. Equivalent: ECOM F242, ECE F242, EEE F242 & INSTR F242: Control Systems.

course_descriptions.title: Signals and Systems
course_descriptions.description: This course is intended to provide a comprehensive coverage of Signals and Systems, a fundamental subject of Electrical Engineering. The topics covered are: Continuous-time and discrete time signals and systems, convolution, properties of linear timeinvariant (LTI) systems, Fourier series, Fourier transform, Z transform, Laplace trans-form; System analysis, frequency response, analog filters, Sampling and reconstruction. Equivalent: ECOM F243, ECE F243, EEE F243 & INSTR F243: Signals and Systems.

course_descriptions.title: Embedded Systems for Robotics
course_descriptions.description: Introduction to Embedded Systems and its Role in Robotics, Microcontroller Basics, ARM Cortex-M Microcontrollers, Embedded Programming on ARM, Communication Protocols in ARM, Introduction to Real Time Operating Systems, Interfacing Sensors and Actuators with Embedded System, Power Management in Embedded systems for Robotics.

course_descriptions.title: Fluid Power Systems
course_descriptions.description: Introduction to Fluid power, advantages of fluid power, ap-plications, Introduction to Pneumatics, Air preparation and Components, Pneumatics Circuits and Applications, Elec-tro pneumatics, Electrical Controls for fluid power circuits, , Physical properties of hydraulic fluids, Energy and Power in Hydraulic Systems, Frictional Losses in Hydraulic Pipe-lines, Hydraulic Pumps, Hydraulic Cylinders and Cushion-ing Devices, Hydraulic Motors, Hydraulic Valves, Hydraulic Circuit Design and Analysis, Ancillary Hydraulic Devices, Hydraulic Conductions and Fittings, Maintenance of Hy-draulic Systems, Use of PLC programming for interfacing pneumatics and Hydraulic Circuits. Equivalent: ME F411: Fluid Power Systems.

course_descriptions.title: Robot Dynamics & Control
course_descriptions.description: Differential Kinematics: Forward and inverse velocity kinematics, and Jacobians for velocity and force mapping. Dynamics: Derivation of equations of motion using the Euler-Lagrange and Newton- Euler formulations. Control of Robotic Manipulators: Trajectory planning, motion control, and advanced control strategies like PID, model-based, and adaptive control. Sensors and Actuators: Integration of sensors and actuators for real-time control. Simulation and Implementation: Practical applications using simulation tools and real-world experiments.

course_descriptions.title: Computer Vision
course_descriptions.description: Introduction to digital image format and camera model with calibration; Image features and its use in classification and segmentation; Multiview geometry, Optical flow and Struc-ture From Motion; Introduction to machine learning for computer vision - Image classification with linear classifi-ers, regularisation and optimization, evolution of hand-crafted feature and classical machine learning models to Convolution Neural Network (CNN) and deep learning; Various deep learning models for multiple tasks: CNN (classification), Deconvolutional Network (segmentation), Recurrent Neural Networks with LSTM (Long Short Term Memory) and GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit) for video analy-sis, Attention and Transformers for image and video, Self supervised learning, Generative models, 3D vision. Equivalent: BITS F459: Computer Vision.

course_descriptions.title: IoT for Industrial Automation
course_descriptions.description: Industry 4.0 and industrial automation, Key drivers of industrial IoT (IoT, AI, cloud computing, and big data analytics), IoT architecture, Fundamentals of industrial automation, Components of automation systems, Sensors and actuators for automation, IoT hardware and software, Networking and communication in industrial IoT, Cybersecurity for industrial IoT, Intelligent devices and VIautonomous systems, Industrial data acquisition and data analytics, Wireless communication standards, Industrial identification technologies, IoT protocols for industrial communication, Cloud computing for industrial IoT, Edge computing and real time processing, Smart monitoring systems for production floors, Machine-to-Machine communication, IoT enabled automation for smart manufacturing, Industrial IoT for predictive and preventive maintenance, IoT-enabled robotics, Connected manufacturing environments, Digital twins for automation, Integration of IoT with legacy industrial systems, Case studies and implementation strategies, IoT based automation solutions.

course_descriptions.title: Computer-Aided Design
course_descriptions.description: Mathematical modeling of parametric curves, surfaces and solids. Geometric transformations, isometric transformations including translation, scaling, reflection, and rotation using specialized solid modeling packages. CAD/CAM data exchange. Introduction to FEM & FEA practice on a specialized CAE package. Modeling and simulation based practical exercises related to geometric modeling, finite element analysis, and machine drawing such as orthographic drawing, sectional view, assembly drawing & exploded view. Equivalent: ME F318: Computer-Aided Design

course_descriptions.title: Autonomous Mobile Robotics
course_descriptions.description: Kinematics, Dynamics and Control of Mobile Robots, Path planning, Roadmaps, Cell decomposition, Sensors for mobile robots, Sensor fusion algorithms, Autonomous navigation algorithms. Equivalent: BITS F451: Autonomous Mobile Robotics.

course_descriptions.title: Industrial Automation & Control
course_descriptions.description: Introduction of Industrial Automation, Process Control Systems & Instrumentation, Advanced Control Strategies, Automation in Process Industries: PLC fundamentals, programming & applications, PLC Code Automation and Logic Extraction, Distributed Control System, Supervisory Control and data acquisition systems, Piping & Instrumentation Diagram, Condition Monitoring ,Safety, Standards, recent trends and future of industrial automation, Modular Automation and Industry 4.0, Digital Twin Technology, Case studies and applications.

course_descriptions.title: Underwater Robotics
course_descriptions.description: Underwater robotic systems, Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs), Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs), underwater gliders, and Argo floats; concepts of dynamics, control, navigation, and path planning; designing and integrating the fundamental elements of underwater robots, including vehicle parameters like pressure, buoyancy, power, speed, and range; Kinematics, guidance, and navigation strategies, dead-reckoning and SLAM, A* and line-of-sight (LOS) guidance; PID controllers and thruster design, applications in remote sensing, environmental monitoring, biomimetic robotics, and real-world case studies from various countries.

course_descriptions.title: Autotronics and Vehicle Intelligence
course_descriptions.description: Testing and validating automotive electronic systems using modern software and hardware tools; Autotronics systems; automotive electronics systems and subsystems; hybrid vehicles and intelligent vehicle systems, future advancements in automotive electronic technologies.

course_descriptions.title: AR/VR in Robotics
course_descriptions.description: A foundational course on leveraging AR/VR for advanced robotics applications, design and interaction. Enhancement of the capabilities of robotic systems using AR/VR technologies; robot simulation, immersive teleoperation and enhanced visualization.

UrbanDrainage and Sewerage, Carbon, nitrogen andphosphorus removal & recovery; sludge treatment, Siteevaluation; toilets; onsite sanitation systems; emptyingand transport; established and transferring technologiesfor dewatering, stabilization, pathogen inactivation andnutrient management, urban low cost drainage,Innovation processes, Intro & Exercise technologyselection tool / decision support system; discussoutcomes.

course_descriptions.description: Change andAdvocacy This particular course will have two modules –Sanitation Governance and Behaviour change &Advocacy. Water & sanitation governance: definitions, debates, controversies, Power relations among actorsin the local and global levels: Gender, class & racerelations and power asymmetries, Practices ofcoordination & decision, making around contestedwater distribution, Case studies on regulatoryframeworks around the world – how is sanitationmanaged: where, how and why, Everyday sanitationfrom different perspectives. Behaviour with referenceto Societal and cultural aspects, Types: Knowledge,motivations and reactions, Reinforcements: Norms andbehaviour Settings

course_descriptions.title: Sanitation Financing and Project Manage-
course_descriptions.description: ment This course will have two modules – SanitationFinancing and Project Management. Introduction tofinancial viability, CAPEX, OPEX, business modelsand PPP of sanitation project, Calculating CAPEX andOPEX of a sanitation project and developing abusiness model, Local authority/municipal budgetingand public/government financing, Key aspects ofproject management including stakeholders’relationship, people management, risk management,budget management, reporting, Objective OrientedProject Planning.

course_descriptions.title: Emergency Sanitation and Leadership
course_descriptions.description: This course will have two modules – EmergencySanitation and Leadership. The evolution ofhumanitarian aid: historical events and thehumanitarian system as it stands today. Overview ofthe international legal framework (Refugee law, International Humanitarian Law-IHL, InternationalDisaster Relief Law-IDRL), code of conduct andguiding principles of humanitarian action. Standardsapplied by relief agencies and global cluster, Sphere, WASH cluster. Disaster cycle, risk reduction/response/ recovery/ development, emergency responsephases. Overview of relief organizations, theirmandates, their commitments and priorities inemergencies. VI-

course_descriptions.title: Sanskrit
course_descriptions.description: Simple pieces of Sanskrit prose and poetry to be used for teaching the basic construction of Sanskrit words and sentences. The course will aim at making the student read elementary Sanskrit like a Subhashita Sloka or a Sloka from Ramayana or Mahabharata and be able to understand it with the help of a dictionary.

course_descriptions.title: Research Methodology II
course_descriptions.description: These two courses, to be offered in two consecutive semesters, are designed to impart training in methodology of research such as analysis of research problems, mathematical and statistical analysis of data, computer simulation methods, experimental techniques etc. The actual contents of these courses will depend upon the needs and research goals of a particular student. A project report has to be submitted by each student at the end of each course. The organisation and evaluation of these courses would be achieved through seminars, group discussions, project reports etc. The courses will be conducted by a team of teachers. Note: All the above mentioned Skill courses will be 'Unstructured' in the sense that they would be completely of 'non- lecture, type but would require committed involvement in the concerned professional engagement. Each course is a combination of two course numbers I & II running in two successive semesters where grades would be awarded for the two components separately. While normally a student will be required to take I & II, in rare occasions he may be asked to take only Course No. I depending on his prior preparation and the ultimate goal to be achieved through the programme. No student can register I and II of the same course concurrently in a semester. Where there is sufficient academic justification to meet the goals of these courses, the Dean Instruction may permit delayed registration in course No. II or in the pair of courses. M.Sc. Semiconductor and Nanoscience

course_descriptions.title: Fundamentals of Nanoscience and
course_descriptions.description: Nanotechnology Introduction; nanoscience in nature; fundamental science behind nanomaterials; properties and synthesis of nanomaterials; application of nanomaterials in science, engineering and biomedical field; future trends.

course_descriptions.title: Quantum Mechanics
course_descriptions.description: Origin of the quantum theory - black body radiation, photoelectric effect, Compton scattering, electron diffraction, Bohr model of hydrogen atom, Frank-Hertz experiment, Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization condition; notion of wave function, statistical interpretation of the wave function, issues of normalization, the Heisenberg uncertainty relation; Schrodinger equation, stationary states and time independent Schrodinger equation, energy eigenvalues and eigenfunctions, one-dimensional problems – potential wells, potential barriers, the harmonic oscillator; Hilbert space formalism – state vectors, Dirac’s bra-ket notation, observables as Hermitian operators, eigenvalues and eigenstates of Hermitian operators, the measurement postulate. Equivalent: PHY F242: Quantum Mechanics I

course_descriptions.title: Material Science and Engineering
course_descriptions.description: Introduction on materials for engineering, structures of metals, ceramics and polymers; crystalline structure imper-fections; amorphous and semicrystalline materials (in-cludes glasses, introduction to polymers); Correlation of structure to properties and engineering functions (mechan-ical, chemical, electrical, magnetic and optical); phase diagrams; Improving properties by controlled solidification, diffusion or heat treatment; Failure analysis and non-destructive testing; Types of materials (includes synthesis, Fabrication and processing of materials): Polymers and composites, Environmental degradation of materials (corrosion); Evolution of materials (functional materials, Biomi-metic materials, energy saving materials etc); Criteria for material selection. Equivalent: CHE F243: Material Science and Engineering

course_descriptions.title: Fundamentals of Solid State Physics
course_descriptions.description: Crystal structure and bonding; X-ray diffraction, reciprocal space, Brillouin zone, and structural analysis; Free electron theory of metals; Periodic potential and band theory of solids; Semiconductors- energy band gap and carrier density; Magnetism– Para, Dia and Ferro and Antiferro magnetism, magnetic ordering.

course_descriptions.title: Chemistry at Nanoscale
course_descriptions.description: Nano and nature, importance of nanoscience, chemistry behind nano; instruments for characterizing nanomaterials; diversity in nanosystems: chemical aspects of metallic, magnetic and semiconducting nanomaterials, carbon-based nanomaterials, self-assembled monolayers, monolayer protected metal nano- materials, core-shell nanomaterials; applications of nano materials in catalysis, energy storage and conversion, nanosensors, and biology.

course_descriptions.title: Electronic Devices
course_descriptions.description: Electrical conduction in solids, energy bands in solids, charge carriers in semiconductors, excess carriers in semiconductors, Fabrication of p-n junctions, equilibrium conditions, forward and reverse biased junctions, metal-semiconductor junctions Bipolar junction transistors, field effect transistors (JFET, HEMT, MOSFET), Special diodes (varactor diode, solar cell, LEDs, Tunnel diode and HBT), dielectric materials and insulation (Polarization mechanisms, frequency dependence, dielectric strength and insulation breakdown). Advances on inorganic/organic semiconductor materials and devices for optoelectronic applications such as display, lighting, and lasers. Equivalent: EEE F214: Electronic Devices

course_descriptions.title: Materials & Nanoscale Characterization
course_descriptions.description: Thermal properties of Materials and Characterization, Electrical Characterization: Temperature dependent DC conductivity in materials, impedance spectroscopy, Characterization instruments like impedance analyzer, Mechanical Characterization: Time dependent and time independent mechanical behavior of materials, Dynamic Mechanical Analysis, Universal testing machine, Fatigue machine, impact testers, Hardness indenters, Nanoindentation, Physical Characterization: Microstructure Characterization, SEM, SPM, TEM, X-ray diffraction, SAXS, DLS, UV-PES, Rheological Characterization: Linear and non-linear visco-elastic behavior of materials.

course_descriptions.title: Nanomaterials Synthesis &
course_descriptions.description: Characterization Laboratory The main aim of the course is to build laboratory skills and to provide hands-on experience of various nanomaterial synthesis using both topdown and bottom-up approaches. The course folds in experiments with nanoscale materials. Additionally, the characterization of the synthesized nanomaterials shall be performed. The course is normally available to students of second year and higher levels.

course_descriptions.title: Semiconductor Thin Film Technology
course_descriptions.description: Overview of thin film technology, Structure and bonding of materials, Defects in thin film, Thermodynamics and phase diagram, Kinetics and diffusion mechanism, Surface nu-cleation and film growth, Epitaxy and growth modes, Ba-sics of vacuum science and technology, Thin film growth technology, Epitaxial growth techniques, Structure and morphology of thin films, Surface reconstruction and sur-face chemistry, Electrical and magnetic properties, Special topics on thin film application, Laboratory based experi-ments or assignments related to thin films. Equivalent: PHY F379: Thin Film Technology

course_descriptions.title: Molecular Simulations
course_descriptions.description: Particle based simulations at atomic and molecular level. Molecular dynamics (MD), various algorithms for integrating the equation of motion, Verlet algorithm. Monte Carlo (MC) algorithm, Trial moves, MD and MC in various ensembles, thermostats, barostats etc. Hands-on simulations using GROMACS or LAMMPS or similar. Introduction to density functional theory (DFT), Hands on simulations using any DFT packages such Quantum Espresso or GAUSSIAN or VASP or similar.

course_descriptions.title: Instrumental Methods of Analysis
course_descriptions.description: Principles and practice of modern instrumental methods of chemical analysis. Emphasis on spectroscopic techniques such as UV- Visible, infrared, Raman, NMR (Description: Fundamentals of liquid and solid state techniques), ESR, atomic absorption and emission, photoelectron, Mössbauer, and fluorescence. Other topics will include mass spectrometry, separation techniques, light scattering, electroanalytical methods, thermal analysis, EELS, and Xray Spectroscopies. Equivalent: CHEM F313: Instrumental Methods of Analysis

course_descriptions.title: Nanotechnology & Nanomaterials
course_descriptions.description: in Sensors Use of nanotechnology in sensors capable of performing efficient detection of different types of environmental pollutants. Explore environmental pollution as a threat to life on Earth, the main contaminants (inorganic, organic or pathogens), and the risk they represent to living beings. A brief history of nanotechnology-based sensors; different types of nanotechnology-based sensors (optical, electrochemical, and magnetic); Design and synthesis/fabrication of nanosensors; Carbon-based and noncarbon-based nanomaterials (graphene, carbon nanotubes, quantum dots, magnetic nanomaterials, non-magnetic nanoparticles) and their functionalization to develop nanotechnology-based sensors; Challenges and necessities in sensing environmental pollution, food & agriculture, health, defence, and related domains; Nano- and MEMS-based point-ofcare sensors for chemical, bio, gas, pollution monitoring, and war-field applications; Nanostructured sensors in diverse avenues such as acoustic, piezoelectric, inertial, and thermal; Additional topics on important specific pollutants (pesticides, heavy metal, dyes, toxic gas, pharmaceutical waste, petroleum hydrocarbons, and pathogenic microbes) and their detection by nanotechnology-based sensors; Sensors combined with Internet of Things.

course_descriptions.title: Principles of Nanobiotechnology
course_descriptions.description: The course deals with the principles and applications of biotechnology at the nanoscale (DNA Nanotechnology, Protein Nanotechnology & Microbial Nanotechnology). (Description: Role of nanobiotechnology in the area of infectious & non-infectious diseases). The course includes interdisciplinary aspects of biology and nanotechnology such as nanopharmaceutics, drug delivery systems, and nanofertilizers in the agricultural sector. (Description: Delivery vehicles, nano-drugs, nanomaterials in health sector, targeted drug delivery, theranostics). Interactions of nanosystems with molecular and cellular level for biomedical and biological research applications.

course_descriptions.title: Principles of Nanophotonics and Devices
course_descriptions.description: Foundation of nanophotonics: Similarities and differences between photons and electrons, confinement and propagation of photons and electrons, nanoscale optical interaction etc.; Photonic crystals: Photonic crystal and periodic nanostructures, theoretical band structure, fabrication methods, phonic crystal fiber and communication; Optical properties metallic nanostructures/ Plasmonics: Metallic nanoparticles, nanorods, nanoshells, local field enhancement, plasmonic waveguide; Growth of photonic nanomaterials and nanocomposite: Epitaxial growth, chemical vapor deposition, laser assisted vapor deposition, colloidal synthesis and their spectroscopic and microscopic characterizations, nanocomposite waveguides etc.; Nanofabrication of photonic devices: Two photon and near filed lithography, non-linear optical process, VIplasmatic printing, nanoimprint lithography etc.; Application of nanophotonic materials and devices: Sensing applications, biological applications, optical communications, nanomedicine etc.,

course_descriptions.title: Advanced Nanofabrication
course_descriptions.description: The lab experiments are configured to study the complete flow of designing and testing of nanomaterials-based devices for electronic and sensing applications. The lab will start with an introductory discussion on the process flow and essential instrumentation involved to complete the fabrication steps and testing of the devices. Necessary hands-on training will be provided on substrate preparation and design/transfer of different pattern in sub-micron range by photolithography technique. Training will be provided on different metallization techniques which involves DC sputtering, ebean evaporation and thermal deposition. Two or three terminal electronic devices will be fabricated by transferring active nanomaterials layer on electrode deposited substrate. Appropriate packaging steps will be followed to place nano-devices on suitable chip carrier to facilitate the testing process. The basic electrical characterizations will be performed by measuring the I-V, C-V and FET characteristics of the devices. A few fabricated sensors will also be tested for real time applications like gas sensing and photodetection, etc.
