course_descriptions.title: Physics and Modelling of
course_descriptions.description: Semiconductor Devices Physics and properties of semiconductor - a review; Basics of Semiconductors, Band and Bond model of solids; Thermal-equilibrium statistics, photogeneration and Quasi-Fermi levels; Free Carriers in semiconductors, scattering, velocity saturation. pn junction diode; Graded impurity distributions, Quasi-Neutrality Approximation; depletion layer model; Heterojunction; p-n junction under bias; junction breakdown; Current-Voltage Characteristics of pn junction. Bipolar transistor; Operation; I-V characteristics; Gummel number, high level injection effect, current gain, heavy doping effect; Ebers-Moll Model; Early effect & Charge control model. Metal-semiconductor contacts; Equilibrium in electronic systems, idealized metal semiconductor junctions: Band diagram; C-V Characteristics: Schottky contacts and ohmic contacts. JFETand MESFET; p-n junction Devices: JFET & MESFET. MOSFET and scaling; MOS structure and analysis of the ideal MOS structure; MOS Capacitance; Non-ideal MOS system: Oxide charges in MOS; Gradual channel approximation, body effect, MOSFET I-V Model, subthreshold conduction; Improved models for short channel MOSFETs; Mobility degradation; velocity saturation. Semiconductor Device Modeling & Simulation Lab: This laboratory offers introduction to semiclassical and some aspects of quantum modeling and simulation of semiconductor devices. With emphasis on a variety of semiclassical numerical methods, this simulation-lab provides basic concepts and design tools for analyzing discrete one/two/threedimensional devices such as pn (hetero)junction, Schottky diodes, JFETs, MESFETs, MOSFETs, etc. Silvaco TCAD software will be used for the simulation lab.

course_descriptions.title: Study Project
course_descriptions.description: These courses include projects which are oriented towards readings from published literature or books about new frontiers of development or analysis of available database. These courses are normally available to students in second or higher levels. These courses must coterminate with project reports.

course_descriptions.title: Laboratory Project
course_descriptions.description: These courses include projects involving laboratory investigation or laboratory development in the student’s discipline or interdisciplinary areas. These courses are normally available to students in third or higher levels. These courses must coterminate with project reports.

course_descriptions.title: Laboratory Project
course_descriptions.description: These courses include projects involving laboratory investigation or laboratory development in the students’ discipline or interdisciplinary areas. These courses are normally available to students in third or higher levels. These courses must coterminate with project reports.

course_descriptions.title: Design Project
course_descriptions.description: These courses are intended to impart training in design of product/process or other artifact to the students in the discipline or interdisciplinary areas. These courses are normally available to students in third or higher levels. These courses must coterminate with project reports.

course_descriptions.title: Design Project
course_descriptions.description: These courses are intended to impart training in design of product/process or other artifact to the students in the discipline or interdisciplinary areas. These courses are normally available to students in third or higher levels. These courses must coterminate with project reports.

course_descriptions.title: Special Project
course_descriptions.description: This is an unstructured open-ended course where under the overall supervision of an instructor-in-charge, batches of students will be attached to different instructors. Each batch will work on a specific timebound project which is of basic or peripheral concern of his discipline. Each student must submit a project report as a culmination of his endeavour and investigation. The instructor- incharge will determine the choice of the project and also whether or not the project report is to be submitted jointly by a group or individually by a student. The course will aim to evaluate student's actual ability to use the fundamentals of knowledge and to meet new unknown situations as demonstrated by the students' interaction with the instructors and instructor-in- charge and aggregated in the project report. The instructor-in- charge may assign specific hours for formal brain-storming sessions.

course_descriptions.title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
course_descriptions.description: Design techniques such as divide-and-conquer, recursion, backtracking, branch-and-bound, simulation; Analysis in terms of average level and worst level efficiency; Relationship to appropriate data structures; Illustrations dealing with problems in computer science, graph theory and mathematics; Computational complexity and bounds; NP-hard and NP-complete problems.

course_descriptions.title: Object Oriented Programming
course_descriptions.description: Basics of object oriented programming: objects, classes, instances; inheritance; polymorphism; operator overloading; static and dynamic binding; small talk, C++, cases from other object oriented languages like Ada, Loop, Flavors, Objective-C, etc.; object oriented software engineering.

course_descriptions.title: Network Security
course_descriptions.description: This course examines issues related to network and information security. Topics include security concepts, security attacks and risks, security architectures, security policy management, security mechanisms, cryptography algorithms, securitystandards, security system interoperation and case studies of the current major security systems.

course_descriptions.title: Object Oriented Analysis and Design
course_descriptions.description: Object orientation concepts, theories and principles; fundamental concepts of the object model: classes, objects, methods and messages, encapsulation and inheritance, interface and implementation, reuse and extension of classes, inheritance and polymorphism; process of object-oriented requirements specification, analysis and design; notations for object-oriented analysis and design; case studies and applications using some object oriented programming languages.

course_descriptions.title: Data Warehousing
course_descriptions.description: Introduction, evolution of data warehousing; decision support systems; goals, benefit, and challenges of data warehousing; architecture; data warehouse information flows; software and hardware requirements; approaches to data warehouse design; creating and maintaining a data warehouse; Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) and multi-dimensional data, multi-dimensional VImodeling; view materialization; data marts; data warehouse metadata; data mining.

course_descriptions.title: Computer Organization & Software Systems
course_descriptions.description: Programmer model of CPU; Basic concept of buses and interrupts; Memory subsystem organization; I/O organization; Concept of assembler, linker & loader; Types of operating systems; Concept of process; OS functions: Process scheduling, Memory management, I/O management and related issues.

course_descriptions.title: Data Structures & Algorithm Analysis
course_descriptions.description: Abstract data types; Linear data structures; Hash functions, Binary and other trees, traversal algorithms; Heaps and balanced trees; Sorting and searching techniques; Divide and conquer, recursion, backtracking, branch and bound; Computational complexity and bounds.

course_descriptions.title: Database Design & Applications
course_descriptions.description: DBMS architecture; Data models: Network model, Hierarchical model and Relational model; Database design & optimization; Query processing & Query optimization; Transaction Processing; Concurrency control; Recovery; Security & protection; Introduction to Object Oriented data model & Multimedia Databases.

course_descriptions.title: Social Media Analytics
course_descriptions.description: Basics of social media, its modelling & representation, node classification, community detection, user behaviour, herd behaviour, influence, recommendations in SM, controversy detection, sarcasm detection, fake post detection, behavioural analysis, SM driven problems such as mental health, spreading rumours, etc. Equvalent: CS G519

course_descriptions.title: Advanced Data Mining
course_descriptions.description: Topics beyond conventional record data mining. Mining complex data structures. Tree/graph mining, sequence mining, web/text data mining, stream data mining, spatiotemporal data mining, mining multi-variate time series data, high-dimensional data clustering, and mining social networking sites. Mining data from multiple relations (Multi-relational Data Mining). Privacy preserving Data Mining. Distributed computing solutions for data intensive data mining. SS G521 Fourth Generation Languages and Applica-4 tions Nature of 4GLs; application generators; RDBMS and 4GLs; SQL based 4GLs; 4GLs and development of information systems and decision support systems; other types of 4GLs; case studies.

course_descriptions.title: Software Development Standards
course_descriptions.description: Standards and their role in software development; Institutions involved in formulating and promoting standards; operating environment standards; POSIX; software design standards; diagramming standards; coding standards; language design, code generation and usage standards; software portability and standards; standards in software development tools; standards in compilers and interpreters; open systems; OSI; user interface standards.

course_descriptions.title: Software for Embedded Systems
course_descriptions.description: Real-time and embedded systems; software issues in embedded system; software development process; requirement analysis: use cases, identification and analysis of use cases, use case diagrams; design: architectural design, design patterns and detailed design; implementation: languages, compilers, runtime environments and operating systems for embedded software; testing: methodologies, test cases. The course will also consist of laboratory practices and development of software for embedded systems.

course_descriptions.title: Cloud Computing
course_descriptions.description: Review of Distributed computing - Concurrency, message passing, connectivity and failure models, replication. Computing Infrastructure - Processing Power, Storage aggregation, I/O & Communication, Clusters and Data Centers. Resource modeling and virtualization - CPU virtualization, memory and storage virtualization, virtualized networks. Services - Service models and service contracts; Programming on the cloud. Cloud Applications - Software on the Cloud and Infrastructure Services. Cloud infrastructure - Private vs. Public Clouds, Resource scaling and Resource provisioning. Quality of Service - Performance models, scalability, Performance measurement and enhancement techniques. Security issues - Data/ Storage Security, Resource Access Control, Process Isolation and Control, Service Policies and Privacy Issues.

course_descriptions.title: Pervasive Computing
course_descriptions.description: Select application architectures; hardware aspects; human-machine interfacing; device technology: hardware, operating system issues; software aspects, java; device connectivity issues and protocols; security issues; device management issues and mechanisms; role of web; wap devices and architectures; voice-enabling techniques; PDAs and their operating systems; web application architectures; architectural issues and choices; smart cardbased authentication mechanisms; applications; issues and mechanisms in WAP-enabling; access architectures; wearable computing architectures.

course_descriptions.title: Information Theory
course_descriptions.description: Course description is same as given under BITS G532.

course_descriptions.title: User Interfaces
course_descriptions.description: Increasing knowledge work in organizations; technologies to support growth of knowledge work in organizations; scope, cost, efficiency and reliability of technologies to support knowledge work; role of knowledge in an enterprise; knowledge management process; knowledge management strategies; human aspects of knowledge management; knowledge management technologies; applications of technologies to be covered through cases; reading assignments and use of appropriate software.
course_descriptions.note: description shared with SS G542 (printed once for both)

course_descriptions.title: Knowledge Management
course_descriptions.description: Increasing knowledge work in organizations; technologies to support growth of knowledge work in organizations; scope, cost, efficiency and reliability of technologies to support knowledge work; role of knowledge in an enterprise; knowledge management process; knowledge management strategies; human aspects of knowledge management; knowledge management technologies; applications of technologies to be covered through cases; reading assignments and use of appropriate software.

course_descriptions.title: Advanced Compilation Techniques
course_descriptions.description: Generic Code Optimization Techniques - loop optimization, inlining, and other transformations. Impact of architectures on code generation and optimization: RISC architectures, VLIW architectures, special-purpose architectures. Architecture-specific code optimizations – register allocation, instruction scheduling. Code Optimizations under real-time / embedded constraints - cacheless / diskless memory models, bounded time responses. Garbage Collection Techniques. Virtual Machines and Just-in-Time Compilation techniques - HotSpot-like optimizations. Implementation of exception handling, concurrency, and generic jumps (like call/cc).

course_descriptions.title: Software Testing Methodologies
course_descriptions.description: Concepts and principles of software testing and quality assurance; software testing tools, functional, structural, integration and system testing techniques; software testing process and its management; evaluation of test effectiveness; testing specialized systems and applications; automated software testing; case studies.

course_descriptions.title: Distributed Data Systems
course_descriptions.description: Distributed File Systems - File System Models; Replication and Synchronization - Caching; Failure & Recovery; File System Security. Distributed Databases - Distributed Data Sources and Updates; Database Connectivity; Concurrency Control and Distribution mechanism; Distributed indexing schemes. Database security. Data on the Web - Web as a distributed data repository. Data Collection and Use Crawlers, Search Engines, and Indexing Schemes. Information Retrieval Techniques. Data Exchange - Hierarchical Data Models, XML, and query languages. Semi-structured / Unstructured data -querying and synchronization. Pervasive Data - Data distribution and access for non-computing devices, small computing devices, embedded computing devices and sensory devices.

course_descriptions.title: Software Engineering & Management
course_descriptions.description: Current concepts, methods, techniques, and tools of the software engineering process; software process models; process definition VIand assessment; software measurement and metrics; project planning, estimation and control; requirements analysis and specification, design methods; quality assurance and testing; configuration management; process improvement; case studies and project work.

course_descriptions.title: Computer Based Simulation and Modlling
course_descriptions.description: Discrete event simulation on computers; Systems simulation & simulation languages; GASP & GPSS; Continuous simulation - languages and modelling techniques; Forrester's models; case studies. SS G641 Management Information and Decision Sup-5 port Systems Data & information; characteristics of information; components of management information systems; information flows; design and maintenance of management information systems; decision support systems.

course_descriptions.title: Project Formulation and Preparation
course_descriptions.description: This course is designed to inculcate principles of technical documentation as required within S&T organizations. Through this course, students are expected to acquire familiarity with several of the following: Proposals, feasibility reports, formal project reports, short reports, memos, negotiations, contracts, etc. In the process principles of project formulation and evaluation, such as technical considerations; performance specifications; preliminary block diagrams, types and analysis of contracts; cost estimation concepts, work breakdown structure; project data preparation, scheduling facilities etc., would be introduced. The course would invariably include the preparation of a detailed report embodying as many of the above concepts as appropriate.

course_descriptions.title: Software Architectures
course_descriptions.description: Systems engineering and software architectures; Hatley-Pirbhai architectural template; architecture flow diagrams; requirements engineering and software architecture; architectural design processes; design post-processing; real-time architectures; architectural design patterns; software architecture and maintenance management; object oriented architectures; client-server architectures; forward engineering for object oriented and client-server architectures; emerging software architectures.

course_descriptions.title: Mathematical Foundations of Quantum
course_descriptions.description: Theory Pure states in quantum theory: projective Hilbert space as the space of quantum states, finite and infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces, bases and Gram-Schmidt orthogonalisation. Observables in quantum theory: operators on Hilbert space, Hermitian operators, commutators and anti-commutators, diagonalisation, measurement and eigenvalues, spectral representation, expectation and variance, Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, generalised uncertainty principle. Evolution in quantum mechanics: unitary operators, Hamiltonian and generation of time translations, the Schrodinger and Heisenberg time evolution equations. Composite systems and direct product spaces, Riesz representation theorem, entanglement. Mixed states and density operators, partial trace and subsystems Evolution of continuous variable systems: Partial differential equations and Sturm-Liouville theory, special functions Introductory Lie algebras and group theory. Basic probability theory (Review): random variables and probability distributions, expectation, variance and higher moments, conditional probability and Bayes' theorem, law of large numbers.

course_descriptions.title: Quantum Computation and Information
course_descriptions.description: Bits and qubits, the difference, representation of qubits on the Bloch sphere, Elementary qubit operations: gates, entanglement and teleportation, quantum circuits; Basic quantum algorithms: Deutsch-Josza, Period finding, phase estimation, factorisation, Grover search algorithm, quantum counting; Basic quantum communication, dense coding, quantum secret key distribution; qubit sampling, optimisation algorithms; continuous variable techniques. Error correction and fault tolerance. Information and entropy, von Neumann entropy and its characteristics, Renyi entropy, entropic relations.

course_descriptions.title: Overview of Hardware for Quantum technologies
course_descriptions.description: Superconducting framework, Josephson Junction, Cooper Pair box qubit, 1-qubit gate, transmon qubits and 1-2 qubit gates, readout and initialisation for computing. Semiconductor-based preliminary physics, electron spin qubits in semiconductors, phase shift gates, Rabi oscillations, one qubit and two qubit gates. Single-photon and squeezed/entangled light sources, Qubit encoding, Single and two-qubit gates, Detectors, Applications to computing, communication and sensing. Neutral atom, optical lattice, laser technology, Rydberg atoms, controlled operations and measurement, scalability and topology. Trapped Ion preliminaries, Paul-trap, ion-trap architecture, single qubit control, multiqubit control, beyond conventional qubits. Applications and software, hybrid implementation.

course_descriptions.title: Quantum Communication and Networking
course_descriptions.description: Classical and Quantum Information Theory Fundamentals, Studies on Classical and Quantum Entropies, Information Measures, Quantum entanglement; Applications in various quantum information processing protocols like teleportation, dense coding; Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), Entanglement distribution, Quantum Relays and Repeaters, Quantum Memories, Quantum Detection and Quantum Communication, Quantum Error Correction, Quantum Stabilizer Codes, Quantum communications networks and the quantum Internet, Classical and Quantum Networks, Protocols for Quantum Internet, Fault Tolerant Quantum

course_descriptions.title: Experimental Techniques for Quantum
course_descriptions.description: Technologies Measurement of physical properties, units, and standards. Methods of error analysis, curve fitting, interpolation/extrapolation, and interpretation of data; Basic electronics; Microscopy: Scattering Experiments used for material characterisation: Vacuum techniques; Thin film deposition techniques, Exfoliation techniques and Van der Waals stacking for layered materials; Wire bonding; Device fabrication; Cryogenics; Superconducting magnets; Optics; Optical lattice, laser cooling. This course will also involve a basic lab.

course_descriptions.title: Quantum Algorithms and Applications
course_descriptions.description: Application in Inverse Function Computation, Bernstein–Vazirani and Grover’s Algorithm, Number-theoretic Applications, Phase estimation, Order-finding and factoring, Quantum Fourier transform, Shor’s Factoring Algorithm, Optimization and Approximation Application, Variational Quantum Eigensolver, Quantum Approximation and Optimization Algorithms (QAOA), Quantum Walks, Minimum Spanning Tree, Maximum Flow, Algebraic Applications, Linear Systems, HHL Algorithm, Quantum Matrix Algorithms, Learning Applications, Quantum Principal Component Analysis(PCA), Quantum Support Vector Machines(SVM), Simulating Hamiltonian dynamics, Fast quantum simulation algorithms, Quantum signal processing; adiabatic quantum, computing, Hands-on exposure to platforms like Qiskit (IBM), CUDA-Quantum (NVIDIA), Amazon Braket, and similar toolkits

course_descriptions.title: Introduction to Quantum Materials
course_descriptions.description: Solid state physics and the context of advanced materials: Topological insulators and semimetals; SSH model: Polyacetylene, first example of topological phase transition; Graphene: Monolayer, bilayer, twisted bilayer and other Moire systems; Spin orbit coupling and exotic surface states; Quantum Hall effect, Chern number; Quantum well systems and 2D systems such as graphene and transition metal dichalcogenides; Quantum dots - Single photon emitters and detectors, Single electron transistor; Spintronic materials; Theoretical techniques like Fermionic manybody theory: Tight binding description for electronic dispersion in crystals, Berry’s Phase, Elements of algebraic topology. Micro and Nanofabrication - NEMS TECHNOLOGY - Lithography and device patterning, Low temperature and high magnetic field Measurement techniques - Investigating electrical, magnetic and optical properties; Quantum computing using single photons and ion traps; Quantum computing using superconductors. Superconducting Qubits.

course_descriptions.title: Quantum Cryptography and Security
course_descriptions.description: Quantum Key Distribution, BB84 protocol, Probability Notations, Density Matrices, Partial Trace, Quantum money, Entanglement, Purification, Bell Non-Locality, Quantifying information, Distributing keys, Secure Key Distribution, Quantum Cryptography using untrusted devices, Quantum cryptography beyond key distribution, Coin Flipping, Two-Party Cryptography, Bit Commitment, Security from physical assumptions, Delegated computation.

course_descriptions.title: Atomic and Optical Technology
course_descriptions.description: Basic atomic models: Rutherford’s model, Bohr’s model, Sommerfeld’s model. One-electron atom: Schrodinger equation in spherical coordinates, Separation of variables. Hydrogen atom, Hydrogen spectrum, Rydberg atom. Interaction of electromagnetic field with atoms: Transition rates, dipole approximation, Einstein coefficients, selection rules and spectrum of one-electron atom, line intensities and shapes, line widths and lifetimes, Stark effect, Spin-orbit coupling and fine structure, Normal and anomalous Zeeman effect, Hyperfine structure. Two and multi-electron atoms: Helium atom, Para and ortho states, level scheme, ground and excited states of two-electron atoms. Central field approximation, L-S coupling, j-j coupling. Laser fundamentals: Rate equations, Gain mechanisms, Optical resonators, Q-factor, Cavity modes. Resonant light-atom interaction: Rabi model, Jaynes- Cummings model, Collapse and revival structure, Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT), Dressed States, Autler-Townes Effect. Special optical techniques: Mach-Zehnder interferometer, Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometer, Quantum eraser, Hanbury- Brown-Twiss interferometer, Single photons. Nonlinear optical techniques: Spontaneous parametric down conversion, Secondharmonic generation, Four-wave mixing, Photon detectors. Modern optical techniques: Optical cooling, Optical trapping, Bose- Einstein condensation, Coherent control, Magneto-optical traps (MOT), Optical metrology, Frequency comb, Atomic clocks.

course_descriptions.title: Quantum computing applications using
course_descriptions.description: NISQ devices Search for use-cases for quantum computing, deciding a suitable platform and architecture, algorithm development - state preparation, error mitigation, time evolution, measurement, classical post processing, analyzing errors, benchmarking with classical computing.

course_descriptions.title: Open Quantum Systems
course_descriptions.description: The density matrix formalism for the states of an open quantum system; measurement and probability distributions on an open system; dynamics of an open system - the quantum Master equation, the Lindbladian; dynamical maps and quantum evolution; non-Markovian evolution, non-Hermitian Hamiltonians; Stochastic approach to evolution of open quantum systems.

course_descriptions.title: Quantum Algorithms
course_descriptions.description: Quantum circuits; quantum algorithms for algebraic problems: The abelian quantum Fourier transform and phase estimation, discrete log and the hidden subgroup problem, the abelian HSP and decomposing abelian groups, quantum algorithms for number fields, Period finding from ℤ to ℝ, quantum query complexity of the HSP, Fourier analysis in nonabelian groups, Fourier sampling, Schur-Weyl duality, Approximating the Jones polynomial; quantum walk: Continuous-time quantum walk, discrete-time quantum walk, Unstructured search, quantum walk search; quantum query complexity: query complexity and the polynomial method, Learning graphs, compressed oracle method; quantum simulation: Simulating Hamiltonian dynamics, Fast quantum simulation algorithms, Quantum signal processing; adiabatic quantum computing: quantum adiabatic theorem, adiabatic optimization, an example of the success of adiabatic optimization, Universality of adiabatic quantum computation.

course_descriptions.title: Tensor Network Methods for simulating
course_descriptions.description: quantum computation State-of-the-art calculation techniques based on classical computers that can efficiently simulate quantum dynamics: tensor structures and network representations like Matrix Product States (MPS), Projected Entangled Pair states (PEPS) and Tree Tensor Networks (TTN)- core mathematical tools and concepts; practical applications of tensor networks in simulating quantum dynamics: computational complexity; resource estimation for quantum algorithms; developing as a tool to benchmark implementation of

course_descriptions.title: Quantum Metrology, Sensing and Imaging
course_descriptions.description: Classical estimation theory: Random variables; Distribution functions; Statistical inference; Likelihood function; Minimum-variance unbiased estimators; Parameter and phase estimation; Biased versus unbiased estimators; Fisher information; Cramer-Rao bound. Quantum estimation theory: Quantum Fisher information (QFI); Symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD); Geometric interpretation of QFI; Bures distance. Fundamental limits: standard quantum limit (SQL); Heisenberg limit (HL); Entangled and squeezed states overcoming SQL; Protocols for achieving HL. Adaptive quantum metrology: Feedback and adaptive measurement strategies; Jordan-Schwinger representation; Bayesian inference. Collective spin system: Coherent spin states; Spin squeezing; One-axis and two-axis twisting models; SATIN scheme; Retrodiction and quantum non-demolition measurements. Multi-parameter quantum sensing: QFI matrix; Holevo bound; Distributed quantum sensing. Quantum sensors in different platforms: Atomic vapour; Cold atom; NV-center; Optomechanical. Quantum imaging: Classical limits of imaging resolution; Quantum lithography and sub-diffraction-limited imaging; Ghost imaging; Entanglement-assisted imaging techniques; Applications in microscopy and remote sensing.

course_descriptions.title: Advanced Quantum Information Theory
course_descriptions.description: Noisy quantum systems and their description using the density operator, information content in a quantum system, the effect of noise on an open system represented by Kraus operators, entropy, joint entropy, relative entropy and mutual entropy; entropic relations; Quantum resource theory and unit protocols; quantum compression and coding; quantum error correction. Measurement and Estimation.

course_descriptions.title: Quantum Control and Interfacing Engineering
course_descriptions.description: Quantum measurement theory, Quantum parameter estimation, Open quantum systems, Quantum trajectories, quantum feedback control, Electromagnetic theory and transmission line theory, Microwave network analysis, Impedance matching and tuning, Microwave resonator, Microwave filters, Active RF and microwave devices, Microwave amplifier design, Oscillators and mixers, Microwave engineering.

course_descriptions.title: Quantum Simulations and Simulators
course_descriptions.description: Quantum Gates, Quantum Circuits, Quantum Universality, Computability and Complexity, Performing Search, Code breaking, Solving Np-complete problems, Quantum simulations, Quantum chemistry, Mathematics on a Quantum Computer, Quantum Error Corrections, Alternative Models of Quantum Computation, Statevector Simulators, Tensor Network Simulators, Density Matrix Simulators and Sparse Simulations, Matrix Product States (MPS), Projected Entangled Pair states (PEPS), and Tree Tensor Networks (TTN, Resource Estimation for Quantum Algorithms, Quantum benchmarking.

course_descriptions.title: Post Quantum Cryptography
course_descriptions.description: Introduction to Post quantum cryptography, Quantum computing, hash-based cryptography, code-based cryptography, lattice based cryptography, isogeny-based cryptography, multivariate public key cryptography, algorithms and hardware or software or

course_descriptions.title: Quantum Advanced Programming,
course_descriptions.description: Compilation Models and Frameworks (including HPC) Application of Quantum Computing, In-sequence processing, Single-circuit applications, ensemble-circuit applications, macro-architecture design, micro-architecture design, Quantum Programming Languages and Models. Compilation and Program Optimization Techniques, Quantum Parallel Programming, Quantum- Classical Hybrid Machine Programming, Circuit Cutting techniques

course_descriptions.title: Quantum Software and Application
course_descriptions.description: Development Lifecycle Quantum software development life cycle, Classical and quantum data pipelines, Case studies: Quantum Applications in Finance; Quantum-enabled Supply Chain Optimization; Use cases in Material Science and Drug Discovery; Hands-on exposure to platforms like Qiskit (IBM), CUDA-Quantum (NVIDIA), Amazon Braket, and similar toolkits

course_descriptions.title: Field Theoretical Understanding of
course_descriptions.description: Condensed Matter Physics Second quantisation of many-body systems: non-relativistic/ Schrodinger field theory, free scalar and Dirac field theory. Single particle and multi-particle spectrum of the simple tight-binding model. Symmetries and conservation laws: Noether's theorem, application to free scalar continuum field theories for space-time symmetries, application to discrete models for internal symmetries, roles of symmetries in classifying particles and super selection sectors. Symmetry breaking and collective phenomena: Mean field theory, Bose–Einstein condensation (optional) and superfluidity, Superconductivity, Field theory of the disordered electron gas Renormalisation Group: The one-dimensional Ising model, General set-up of RG, Critical behaviour, Ferromagnetic transition, Non-linear sigma model, BKT transition (optional). Band topology: Berry phase and Chern number, Integer Quantum Hall Effect, Topological Insulator: SSH and Kane-Mele models.

course_descriptions.title: Quantum Error Correction
course_descriptions.description: Density Matrices, Trace, Partial Trace, No cloning Theorem, Quantum Noise Models, Quantum Codes, Knill-Laflamme conditions, Pauli Error Basis, Discretization of Quantum Errors, Shor’s Code, CSS codes, Stabilizer Codes, Clifford Group, Topological Codes (surface codes, color codes), Quantum LDPC codes, Quantum Hamming Bound, Quantum Singleton Bound, Quantum Gilbert-Varshamov Bound, Entanglement Assisted Quantum Error Correction Codes, Fault Tolerant Quantum Computations, Traversal Gates, Faulty tolerant state preparation, Magic states, Threshold Theorem.
